papers.title: An AI-Enabled Translational Drug Discovery Framework for NALCN Channelopathy: From High-Throughput Screening to Therapeutic Candidate
papers.abstract: Background: More than 90% of rare diseases lack an approved therapy, partly reflecting economic barriers in developing treatments for small patient populations. A common bottleneck is costly and resource-intensive hit-to-lead prioritization. Congenital contractures of the limbs and face, hypotonia, and developmental delay (CLIFAHDD) is an ultra-rare neurodevelopmental disease often caused by de novo gain-of-function variants in the sodium leak channel NALCN, with no approved treatments. Methods: We developed a cost and resource-efficient, AI-enabled translational drug discovery framework integrating phenotypic high-throughput screening (HTS), structural biology foundation models for hit-to-lead prioritization, and orthogonal experimental validation. We applied this framework for drug repurposing to identify NALCN inhibitors as therapeutic candidates for CLIFAHDD. We screened ~1,200 approved drugs using a fluorescence-based membrane potential assay in doxycycline-inducible HEK293 cells stably expressing the NALCN channelosome. Boltz-2 modeling predicted binding affinity and mode to prioritize hits. Lead repurposing candidates were selected by a multidisciplinary expert review panel. Lead candidates were evaluated using patch-clamp electrophysiology in HEK293 cells expressing wild-type or CLIFAHDD-associated NALCN variants, primary mouse hippocampal neurons, and a C. elegans NALCN gain-of-function model. Results: HTS identified 11 candidate NALCN inhibitors. Boltz-2 prioritized candidates based on predicted binding affinity and predicted binding within the NALCN pore, consistent with a direct pore-blocking mechanism. Aprepitant emerged as the lead candidate after multidisciplinary evaluation based on its predicted mechanism, pharmacologic properties, blood-brain barrier penetration, established safety profile, and regulatory approval in children and adults. Patch-clamp electrophysiology confirmed partial inhibition of NALCN-mediated sodium leak currents in HEK293 cells (IC50;=2.22 M), with comparable potency against Cav3.1 (IC50=1.63 M). In primary mouse hippocampal neurons, aprepitant reduced sodium leak currents, hyperpolarized resting membrane potential, and decreased spontaneous firing. Aprepitant rescued hyperlocomotor and dystonic phenotypes in a C. elegans gain-of-function NALCN model. There was notable concordance between AI-predicted hits, phenotypic screening hits, and experimental validation. Conclusion: These findings identify aprepitant as a lead therapeutic candidate for CLIFAHDD, and establish an AI-enabled translational drug discovery framework integrating phenotypic screening, structural modeling, and experimental validation for NALCN channelopathies. This scalable and resource-conscious strategy may accelerate hit-to-lead prioritization and drug discovery for rare and ultra-rare diseases lacking effective therapies.

papers.title: Higher-Order Organization Links Circulating Metabolites to Glucocorticoid Action in Human Adipose Tissue
papers.abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are regulators of metabolism, yet how physiological GC exposure remodels adipose metabolism and its relationship with circulating biomarkers remains poorly understood. In a randomised cross-over study of individuals with primary adrenal insufficiency, near-physiological GC exposure was compared to withdrawal using integrated serum metabolomics, abdominal subcutaneous microdialysis metabolomics, and adipose tissue transcriptomics. GC exposure induced coordinated changes in adipose lipid and amino-acid metabolism. Pathway-level entropy analysis revealed GC-state-dependent transcriptional reorganisation, with concentrated organisation during exposure and diffuse organisation during withdrawal. Integrative hypergraph and topological analyses revealed GC-state-dependent reorganisation of circulating metabolite-adipose tissue relationships, with greater higher-order coordination during exposure. The circulating phenylalanine/kynurenine ratio discriminated GC state, showed the strongest shared connectivity to GC-regulated adipose networks, persisted at midnight and in an independent dose-response study, and exhibited circadian rhythmicity. These findings reveal dynamic GC regulation of adipose metabolism and identify a circulating biomarker with potential to guide personalised GC therapy.

papers.title: Acclimation capacity of two-banded seabream juveniles (Diplodus vulgaris) to port conditions: implications for the role of ports as nursery habitats
papers.abstract: orts are highly anthropized coastal environments characterized by elevated pollution and habitat alteration, posing significant challenges for marine organisms. However, the effects of port conditions on juvenile coastal fish using ports as nurseries remain poorly understood. Here, we combined field sampling and in situ caging experiments to investigate the genetic structure (RAD-seq), physiological condition (growth, lipid content, CYP1A-dependent biotransformation activity), and transcriptomic responses (RNA-seq) of juvenile two-banded sea bream (Diplodus vulgaris) exposed to port conditions. Juveniles from a port site were compared with individuals from two nearby non-port sites (T0), before fish from all populations were caged within the port for one month (T1). The site furthest from the port was slightly genetically differentiated. Port juveniles were larger and fatter at T0 than fish from non-port populations, and all populations showed differential regulation of lipid metabolism, xenobiotic detoxification, hypoxia response, and circadian rhythm pathways between T0 and T1. After one month of caging, weight differences persisted while muscle lipid content sharply declined in all populations. Only juveniles from the site furthest from the port significantly grew between T0 and T1. Port juveniles had a different transcriptional response to caging than non-port juveniles, with a higher expression of genes associated with energy metabolism, while non-port individuals overexpressed genes in detoxification, lipid metabolism, and oncogenic pathways. While we admit limitations related to caging conditions, our results suggest that port conditions strongly influence juvenile fish physiology and transcriptional levels, potentially promoting short-term acclimation strategies that could have long-term consequences for health and survival.

papers.title: A Computational Model Captures Orexin-Dependent Modulation of Memory Consolidation.
papers.abstract: Hippocampal sharp-wave ripple (SWR) events occur during post-experience rest and sleep and play a significant role in memory consolidation. Recent ex vivo studies have found orexin-driven neuromodulatory effects on SWR parameters and proposed that they can influence memory consolidation. Additionally, behavioral studies demonstrate contradictory results regarding orexinergic effects on memory acquisition depending on task structure and intervention time. This inconsistency, along with the diffuse spread of orexin receptors (OXR) in the CA1 and CA3 hippocampus, challenges theoretical interpretation of orexinergic effects on memory. To reconcile this problem, we propose a rate-based model linking orexinergic tone-dependent SWR statistics to memory performance. The model combines an encoding module whose gain scales with the global orexinergic tone with a consolidation module driven by OX2R-specific replay dynamics. The model is based on a plasticity rule that considers SWR events as the unit of induction. Therefore, weight change requires sufficient replay content and depolarizing drive. We observed that, depending on the task structure, encoding-dominant learning benefits discrimination as the orexin drive increases. Consolidation-dominant learning shows a non-monotonic relationship with an internal optimum level of orexinergic tone. This interaction highlights that stronger truncation at higher receptor engagement shortens memory replay and reduces the efficacy of the consolidation process. The model predicts that the optimal regime depends on task complexity reflected in sequence length. Together, these results demonstrate how task demands determine whether increased orexinergic drive enhances or impairs effective consolidation and SWR-dependent replay in the hippocampus.

papers.title: Using the aperiodic slope across learning to predict sleep-based memory consolidation
papers.abstract: Homeostatic mechanisms adjust synaptic strengths to regulate neuronal activity across wake-sleep cycles. Although sleep supports memory consolidation, limited research has explored how sleep-induced homeostatic changes influence memory outcomes in humans. The EEG-derived aperiodic slope (1/f) could be a candidate measure of homeostatic memory processes through its reflection of neural excitation-inhibition balance. In this study, 27 participants learned object-word pairs, and completed an immediate recognition test before either a nap or equivalent wakeful period. Resting-state EEG was recorded, both before and after learning and the interval, to derive changes in aperiodic slope values. A delayed recognition test then assessed whether changes in the aperiodic slope (i.e., homeostatic activity) across learning and the interval predicted memory accuracy and N400 amplitude, an index of stimulus expectancy and recognition. Our study found evidence to suggest homeostatic renormalisation, for the nap condition only, indicated by a shift towards inhibition across sleep which was inversely related to the slope change across learning. Although the aperiodic slope change across the nap and wake intervals did not predict delayed memory accuracy, a shift towards inhibition during learning was beneficial for memory accuracy, only in the nap condition. Similarly, a shift towards inhibition across learning, followed by a shift towards excitation in the nap condition, predicted reduced N400 amplitudes. This suggests that homeostatic renormalisation across the nap influenced model updating and stimulus expectancy. This study provides evidence for a link between synaptic homeostatic processes and memory consolidation, emphasising the importance of encoding-related aperiodic activity in this relationship.

papers.title: Multimodal Glymphatic Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis: Associations with Sleep and Disability
papers.abstract: The glymphatic system is the waste clearance pathway in the central nervous system. Although its dysfunction has been associated with several neurological disorders, its role in multiple sclerosis (MS) remains poorly understood. This system is thought to be particularly active during sleep, yet the relationship between sleep metrics and MRI-derived markers of glymphatic activity has been scarcely explored. In this study, we aimed to perform a multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment of glymphatic function in MS and investigate its association with sleep parameters, clinical disability, disease duration and MRI-derived structural markers. The study included 22 patients (34.3{+/-}10.1 years; 16 female) with relapsing-remitting MS and 26 healthy controls (32.2{+/-}5.7 years; 18 female), all of whom underwent 3.0 Tesla MRI. Glymphatic function was assessed using diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index and global blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) signal-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) coupling. In addition, sleep micro- and macrostructural features, clinical disability, disease duration, along with mean diffusivity (MD), lateral ventricular, choroid plexus volumes and lesion load were evaluated. Patients showed reduced DTI-ALPS index, though this difference became only a trend after controlling for MD. No significant group differences were observed in global BOLD signal-CSF coupling. However, in patients, the weaker coupling was associated with longer total sleep time, lower arousal index, greater disability and lateral ventricle enlargement, whereas the DTI-ALPS index showed no significant correlations with any of the measures. Together, these findings challenge the assumption that DTI-ALPS can serve as a reliable marker of glymphatic function in demyelinating diseases such as MS, where disease-related alterations in white matter microstructure can confound diffusion-based measures. In contrast, gBOLD-CSF coupling showed associations with sleep, clinical disability and structural changes in patients, despite the absence of a significant group-level difference. This finding suggests that gBOLD-CSF coupling may capture individual variability in glymphatic-related dynamics relevant to sleep and the clinical expression of MS.

papers.title: What drives intersubject correlation of EEG during auditory narratives?
papers.abstract: When participants are engaged with auditory narratives, physiological and neural signals exhibit temporal correlations between subjects. The intersubject correlation (ISC) increases when attention is directed to the stories, suggesting that shared neural and bodily dynamics arise from a similar processing of the narratives. In this study, we investigated whether the ISC of the EEG elicited by auditory narratives is driven by low-level acoustic (envelope, spectrogram) and/or higher-level linguistic information (word onset, word surprisal) in two groups of healthy participants during passive, attentive and distracted listening. We use temporal response functions (TRFs) for acoustic, and linguistic features to assess the contribution of each feature to the ISC, measured using correlated component analysis (CorrCA). TRFs derived for acoustic features explained a larger fraction of variance in the EEG than linguistic features and were the main contributors to the ISC. The attention-related increase in ISC was driven by all features. Importantly, word surprisal had an effect on ISC only during active story engagement, with timing and scalp distribution consistent with language processing. Notably, the linear responses captured by TRFs only explained a small amount of the overall ISC, suggesting that ISC is largely driven by nonlinear responses to the narratives. Identifying the factors that drive these common neural responses, is clinically relevant for interpreting EEG ISC exhibited in unresponsive patients. We propose that the combined use of ISC and TRFs has the potential to provide meaningful markers of language processing in patients with disorders of consciousness, and we suggest practical recommendations for implementing these approaches in clinical settings.

papers.title: Human Th17 state classification reveals a selective vulnerability in acylcarnitine metabolism in type 2 diabetes
papers.abstract: Th17 cells are categorized as non-pathogenic (Th17np) and pathogenic (Th17p), states defined primarily in murine autoimmune models. In contrast, studying these states in humans remains difficult because these subsets lack validated identifiers. We developed a nanovial-based single-cell ELISA to isolate cytokine-secreting human Th17 cells and define Th17np vs Th17p cell transcriptional states. These signatures enabled predictive classification and flow-cytometric identification across tissues and diseases. Application of these strategies with single-cell metabolic modeling and functional profiling revealed that Th17np cells predominate in type 2 diabetes yet exhibit impaired fatty acid oxidation capacity despite elevated carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A). CRISPR perturbation and pharmacologic inhibition identified acylcarnitine metabolism as a regulator of Th17 state balance and exposed a selective metabolic vulnerability in type 2 diabetes. This framework links human Th17 cell pathogenicity to lipid metabolism.
